title: Thermal Cycling
introduction: Thermal cycling is a primary environmental stressor driving crack-related degradation in photovoltaic modules. Daily and seasonal temperature variations impose cyclic mechanical loads on bonded dissimilar materials throughout the module stack. When temperature changes, each material expands or contracts according to its coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE), and because bonded materials have different CTEs, cyclic thermo-mechanical stress accumulates at every interface. Over thousands of cycles, this fatigue loading drives crack nucleation in solder interconnects, thin-film interface delamination, and progressive cracking of edge seals.
reasoning: Multiple sources document thermal cycling as the root environmental stressor causing solder joint fatigue cracking, thin-film delamination, and edge seal cracking in PV modules.

key_findings.claim: Cooling below EVA glass transition temperature amplifies CTE mismatch strain energy approximately 100-fold at bonded film interfaces
key_findings.detail: Below the glass-transition temperature (Tg), the elastic modulus of EVA increases dramatically — approximately 100-fold — causing the rate at which thermal mismatch strain energy builds at the laminate interface to accelerate significantly. [^acs011a] Decreasing the quench temperature increases the quench depth relative to the glass-transition temperature, further amplifying the stored strain energy and the driving force for crack initiation. [^acs011b]

key_findings.claim: Real field temperature cycles impose CTE mismatch thermo-mechanical stress on PV solder interconnections, driving fatigue and creep damage
key_findings.detail: Field thermal cycling based on real outdoor temperature monitoring creates daily temperature swings that apply cyclic loads to solder interconnects. [^mdpi1261a] The variation in CTE among silicon, glass, copper, and solder generates thermo-mechanical stresses during each cycle, inducing both fatigue and creep damage in the solder joint over time. [^mdpi1261b]

key_findings.claim: Temperature cycling generates repeated expansion-contraction mismatch at module edges, initiating seal cracking over time
key_findings.detail: Temperature cycles cause thermal expansion and contraction of module components, and because the thermal expansion coefficient of the cover plate and sealant differ, repeated cycling stresses the adhesive bond between them. [^spie1564a] After many cycles of heat expansion and shrinkage, the sealing rubber and cover plate experience adhesive failure. [^spie1564b]
